item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Sharif opposed arms-control, inspection, nonproliferation, or disarmament agreements. I also did not find a 2024 event where he personally signed or announced a new treaty accession. The evidence is mostly institutional and diplomatic, so the safest conclusion is: supportive in posture and engagement, but with limited proof of new ruler-level treaty initiative.","evidence":[{"title":"Arms Control And Disarmament","publisher":"Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan","date":"Standing policy page; current version cites a May 2024 update","url":"https://mofa.gov.pk/arms-control-and-disarmament","summary":"Pakistan’s official policy page says it supports CTBT objectives, a unilateral testing moratorium, FMCT negotiations, IAEA safeguards and reciprocal inspections proposals, UNSCR 1540 implementation, export controls, and non-discriminatory multilateral nonproliferation/disarmament norms. The page also says Pakistan published an updated nuclear-security booklet in May 2024 and joined the Nuclear Security Contact Group. This is the strongest evidence of support, though it is institutional rather than a single Sharif quote.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.3"]},{"title":"Joint Statement on 6th Round of Pakistan-United Kingdom Dialogue on Arms Control & Non-Proliferation","publisher":"Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan","date":"2024-05-16","url":"https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/6th-round-of-pakistan-uk-dialogue-on-arms-control-non-proliferation","summary":"Pakistan and the UK held a formal arms-control and nonproliferation dialogue, reviewed UN, CD, IAEA, and OPCW issues, and pledged continued coordination on multilateral fora. This supports a good-faith engagement reading.","question_ids":["1B.4"]},{"title":"Pakistan-China Bilateral Consultations on Arms Control and Nonproliferation","publisher":"Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan","date":"2024-09-14","url":"https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/pakistan-china-bilateral-consultations-on-arms-control-and-nonproliferation","summary":"Pakistan held the 9th round of consultations on arms control and nonproliferation, covering global/regional security, cyber, AI, outer space, peaceful nuclear technology, and multilateral treaty forums. That is direct evidence of ongoing diplomatic engagement with arms-control mechanisms.","question_ids":["1B.4"]},{"title":"Prime Minister’s participation in the 79th Session of the United Nations General Assembly","publisher":"Press Information Department, Pakistan","date":"2024-09-22","url":"https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/26508","summary":"The government said Sharif would reaffirm Pakistan’s commitment to multilateralism and the UN role in global peace and security at UNGA. This is broader than arms control, but it supports a de-escalatory and institution-first posture.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.2"]},{"title":"The visit of UN Disarmament Fellows to Pakistan","publisher":"Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan","date":"2024-10-21","url":"https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/the-visit-of-un-disarmament-fellows-to-pakistan","summary":"Pakistan hosted UN disarmament fellows and briefed them on its stance on arms control, disarmament, nonproliferation, and its nuclear safety/security architecture. That is direct evidence of active engagement with the disarmament education and verification ecosystem.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.3"]},{"title":"‘Chill of a new Cold War’ is in the air, Pakistan leader tells UN Assembly","publisher":"UN Geneva","date":"2024-09-27","url":"https://www.ungeneva.org/en/news-media/news/2024/09/98067/chill-new-cold-war-air-pakistan-leader-tells-un-assembly","summary":"Sharif’s UNGA remarks framed the global environment as a dangerous new Cold War and emphasized conflict, terrorism, and the need for diplomacy. This is not an arms-control agreement, but it is consistent with de-escalation politics rather than rejection of restraint.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.2"]}]}
